writeup: TIC 97700077 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 3.7702 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse causes a 1.37% dimming of the star's light, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal achieves a detection significance of 55.6 in the BLS periodogram analysis, and pixel-level difference imaging confirms a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 21.9, though the centroid offset of 3.7 arcsec from the target warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it may be a previously unknown system. The machine-learning screening score of 0.21 indicates moderate confidence in this being a real target, and the light curve passes all automated data quality checks.
